writing.exampleCaption: The losing branch is dropped, mid-await, with no warning.
writing.explanation: There is no cancel signal to handle: the future is simply dropped at the next await point, so any state it held runs its destructors and any work in flight stops. That makes cleanup automatic but means a future must be cancel-safe — losing a half-consumed buffer or a partially applied write between awaits is the classic bug.
writing.feedback: The buffer lives in the future, so cancelling drops the read data.
